questions.question: When stopping, what should you do?

options.text: Apply both brakes at the same time.
Use only one brake, either front or rear.

questions.correctAnswerText: Apply both brakes at the same time.
questions.explanation: Use both brakes every time you slow down or stop. Apply them at the same time.

questions.question: If one of your tires goes flat while riding, what should you do?

options.text: Gently apply the brake on the tire that is not flat.
Speed up to leave the road quickly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Gently apply the brake on the tire that is not flat.
questions.explanation: If a tire goes flat, ease off the throttle and stay straight. Slow down gradually. If you must brake, gently apply the brake on the tire that is not flat.

questions.question: Where is the greatest risk of conflict between a motorcycle and other vehicles?
questions.explanation: The greatest risk of conflict happens at intersections. Be extra alert where another vehicle might cross your path.

questions.question: When choosing a helmet, it should have all of the following qualities, except:

options.text: Meet U.S. Department of Transportation standards.

questions.explanation: Choose a helmet that meets U.S. Department of Transportation and state standards. It should fit snugly all the way around and have no obvious defects like cracks, loose padding, or frayed straps.

questions.question: When riding a motorcycle, you should:

options.text: Assume your motorcycle is as easy to see as other vehicles.
Assume other drivers cannot see you.
Not worry about whether other drivers see you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Assume other drivers cannot see you.
questions.explanation: Motorcycles are small and have fewer lights than other vehicles, so they are hard to see. Ride defensively and assume other drivers do not see you.

questions.question: When riding with a passenger, how should you adjust your riding?

options.text: Stay closer to the vehicle ahead than you would without a passenger.
Brake later than you would without a passenger.

questions.explanation: A passenger adds weight. Your motorcycle will need more time to speed up, slow down, and turn. Reduce your speed, start slowing earlier, increase your following distance, and find larger gaps when turning or merging.

questions.question: Where is the engine cut-off switch usually located?
questions.explanation: The engine cut-off switch is usually next to the right handgrip. Learn where all your motorcycle's controls are before you ride.

questions.question: What does this hand signal mean?
questions.explanation: Hand signals show turns or stops instead of or in addition to turn signals. When the left arm is bent at the elbow and points down, it means the rider plans to slow down or stop.

questions.question: Which colors help riders be seen best?
questions.explanation: Wear bright orange, red, yellow, or green clothing to be more visible to other drivers.

questions.question: When making a normal stop, what should you do?

options.text: Use both the front and rear brakes.
Use only the rear brake to save the front brake.
Use only the front brake to save the rear brake.
Squeeze only the front brake hard.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use both the front and rear brakes.
questions.explanation: Use both brakes every time you slow down or stop. If you practice this habit now, it will be easier to use both brakes in an emergency stop.

questions.question: Which of these is NOT protective clothing for motorcyclists?
questions.explanation: A leather jacket, long denim pants, and full-fingered gloves all protect you in a fall. Wear lace-up boots, high-top boots, or heavy shoes with ankle support instead of athletic shoes.

questions.question: Which of these will NOT help reduce your chance of an accident?

options.text: Spotting hazards and deciding which to handle first.

questions.explanation: To avoid crashes, stay alert and ready to react. Watch for hazards and decide what to handle first. Always use your headlight to be more visible. Keep enough space around your motorcycle at all times.

questions.question: Moving into another lane while turning is usually caused by:
questions.explanation: Entering a turn at too high a speed can cause you to cross into another lane or leave the road completely.

questions.question: A pre-ride inspection should:

options.text: Not be done before every ride.

questions.explanation: Check your motorcycle before every ride. A thorough inspection usually takes just a few minutes.

questions.question: The best way to handle a tailgater is usually to:

options.text: Move onto the shoulder to get out of their way.
Speed up to put distance between you and them.
Change lanes and let them pass.

questions.correctAnswerText: Change lanes and let them pass.
questions.explanation: Get the tailgater in front of you. If it is safe, change lanes and let them pass. Speeding up may make them follow you faster and increase danger.

questions.question: To be more visible at an intersection, you should:

options.text: Make eye contact with other drivers.
Ride very close to the vehicle ahead.

questions.explanation: Using your headlight is the most important thing you can do to help others see you at an intersection. Keep your headlight on whenever your motorcycle is running.

questions.question: When you are stopped, you should:
questions.explanation: Shift down through the gears as you slow or stop. Stay in first gear while stopped so you can move quickly if needed.

questions.question: When carrying a passenger or cargo:

options.text: It takes less time to speed up, but more time to stop.
It takes more time to speed up and to stop.
It takes more time to speed up, but less time to stop.
It takes less time to speed up and to stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: It takes more time to speed up and to stop.
questions.explanation: Extra weight from a passenger or cargo makes your motorcycle take longer to speed up and stop than when carrying only the rider.

questions.question: When passing parked cars on your right with no oncoming traffic, you should:

options.text: Stay toward the right side of your lane.
Stay toward the left side of your lane.
Use your rearview mirrors more often than usual.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay toward the left side of your lane.
questions.explanation: When passing parked cars, stay on the side of your lane away from them. This protects you from doors opening or people stepping out. If traffic is coming toward you, stay in the center of your lane.

questions.question: A group of riders should merge onto a highway in:
questions.explanation: A staggered formation is best for normal riding, but switch to single-file when turning, taking curves, or entering or exiting a highway.

questions.question: Making eye contact with another driver:

options.text: Guarantees that the other driver will yield to you.
Does not mean the driver will yield to you.
Means the driver knows you are there.

questions.correctAnswerText: Does not mean the driver will yield to you.
questions.explanation: Never assume that eye contact with another driver means they will yield the right-of-way to you.

questions.question: A motorcyclist is well-protected when wearing:

options.text: A jacket that leaves the arms exposed.
Shoes that do not cover the ankles.

questions.explanation: Wear a jacket and pants that cover your arms and legs. Wear tall, sturdy boots that cover and support your ankles. Choose shoes with low heels to prevent catching on foot pegs. Leather gloves protect your hands in a crash and help you grip the controls better.

questions.question: A benefit of regular motorcycle maintenance is:

options.text: The motorcycle will ride well for a long time.
Maintenance checks take a lot of time.
Maintenance checks can prevent parking tickets.

questions.correctAnswerText: The motorcycle will ride well for a long time.
questions.explanation: A properly maintained motorcycle will continue to ride well. Regular maintenance checks should be part of your motorcycle's care routine.

questions.question: A rectangular sign may be a:
questions.explanation: Regulatory signs like speed limits are rectangular with white backgrounds and black lettering. You must follow the rules shown on these signs.

questions.question: Which of the following protects your eyes from the wind?
questions.explanation: Goggles and face shields protect your eyes from the wind. Windshields, eyeglasses, and sunglasses do not provide enough protection.
